Question: For each positive integer \(n,\) let \(S(n)\) denote the sum of the digits of \(n.\) For how many values of \(n\) is \(n + S(n) + S(S(n)) = 2007?\)
Solution:
The two digit sums are small compared with \(2007\), so first use them to confine \(n\) to a short interval. Both digit sums are positive, giving \(n\le2005\). For \(n\le1999\), its digit sum is at most \(1+9+9+9=28\); for \(2000\le n\le2005\), it is at most \(7\). Thus \(S(n)\le28\). Every positive integer at most \(28\) has digit sum at most \(10\), so
\[
1969=2007-28-10\le n\le2005.
\]

If \(2000\le n\le2005\), write \(n=2000+d\), where \(0\le d\le5\). Then \(S(n)=2+d\) is a single digit, so \(S(S(n))=2+d\). The equation becomes
\[
2004+3d=2007,
\]
which gives \(d=1\) and \(n=2001\).

For the remaining interval \(1969\le n\le1999\), write
\[
n=1900+10a+b,
\]
where \(a\in\{6,7,8,9\}\) and \(b\) is a digit. Then \(S(n)=10+a+b\). Its digit sum depends on whether \(a+b\) reaches \(10\).

If \(a+b\le9\), then \(S(S(n))=1+a+b\). Substitution gives
\[
1911+12a+3b=2007,
\qquad 4a+b=32.
\]
For \(a=6,7,8,9\), respectively, the required values of \(b\) are \(8,4,0,-4\). Only \((a,b)=(8,0)\) satisfies both the digit restrictions and \(a+b\le9\). This gives \(n=1980\).

If \(a+b\ge10\), then \(S(n)=20+(a+b-10)\), so \(S(S(n))=a+b-8\). Now
\[
1902+12a+3b=2007,
\qquad 4a+b=35.
\]
For \(a=6,7,8,9\), the required values of \(b\) are \(11,7,3,-1\). The valid pairs are \((7,7)\) and \((8,3)\), giving \(n=1977\) and \(n=1983\).

The four resulting values satisfy the original equation:
\[
\begin{aligned}
1977+24+6&=2007,\\
1980+18+9&=2007,\\
1983+21+3&=2007,\\
2001+3+3&=2007.
\end{aligned}
\]
The bounds and disjoint digit cases cover every possibility, and each decimal representation is unique. Therefore there are \(4\) values, choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
